pages.text: This tutorial seeks to expand the reader’s notion of spell chaining to projectiles, demonstrating one way in which a projectile might be cast from the impact point of another projectile.$(br2)The following spell will be executed across two pages. It first cast a firebolt, storing the projectile’s direction vector. It then executes a series

of operations on the projectile’s result in order to generate a direction species by which to reflect the original direction vector. Finally, it uses the reflected direction vector and the impact point position vector to cast a second firebolt, creating a ricochet effect.

pages.title: I: Ricochet Firebolt
pages.text: Casts a firebolt, saving its direction vector onto the tag and cloning the impact position twice, leaving three species for the impact position vector on the capsum.

1) Gets the caster’s position.$(br2)2) Gets the caster’s look vector and saves a copy of this species onto the tag.$(br2)3) Casts the firebolt and retrieves the vector position from the impact result.$(br2)4) Duplicates the vector twice, meaning the capsum contains three copies of the impact position vector.

pages.title: II: Ricochet Firebolt
pages.text: Uses the three impact position results, to cast a second firebolt from the impact point that emulates a ricochet.

5) Gets the block position of the block hit, and then gets the direction matching the face hit (up/north/east).$(br2)6) Reads the tag, pushing the original direction vector onto the head, and swaps. Then reflects the vector by the direction species.$(br2)7) The capsum contains the reflected vector and a copy of the impact position vector. Pushes an integer and completes the firebolt cast.
